record.original_question: Which pairs of polytopes P and Q have a nonempty amalgamation class hP, Qi for which the number of flag orbits among polytopes in hP, Qi is bounded?

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Classify all pairs of polytopes P and Q such that hP, Qi is non-empty and the number of flag orbits of polytopes in hP, Qi is bounded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $P$ (with a least and greatest element) whose elements, called faces, are ranked $-1, 0, 1, \dots, n$, satisfying the usual diamond, flag-connectedness, and strong flag-connectedness conditions of abstract polytope theory. A flag of $P$ is a maximal chain of faces. The automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(P)$ acts on the set of flags, and the number of orbits of this action is called the number of flag orbits of $P$.

For an $(i-1)$-face $F$ and an $(i+1)$-face $G$ of $P$ with $F < G$, the section $G/F = \{H \in P : F \le H \le G\}$ is itself an abstract polytope. Given two abstract polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ (of rank $n-1$) and $\mathcal{Q}$ (of rank $n-1$), the amalgamation class $\langle \mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}\rangle$ is defined as the class of all abstract polytopes $\mathcal{R}$ of rank $n$ such that every facet (maximal proper face section) of $\mathcal{R}$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{P}$ and every vertex-figure of $\mathcal{R}$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{Q}$.

Problem. Classify all pairs of abstract polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ such that the amalgamation class $\langle \mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}\rangle$ is non-empty and there exists a uniform finite upper bound on the number of flag orbits of the polytopes belonging to $\langle \mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}\rangle$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published classification of pairs $(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$ for which the amalgamation class has a bounded number of flag orbits was found. The amalgamation problem and related flag-orbit questions remain a topic of active study (e.g., work on two-orbit polytopes, chiral extensions, and few-flag-orbit polytopes by Hubard, Pellicer, Schulte, Matteo, and others), with no source indicating a complete answer to this classification.

status_evidence.title: Convex Polytopes and Tilings with Few Flag Orbits (Matteo)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies polytopes by their number of flag orbits, indicating it remains a structural classification problem.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of polytopes by number of flag orbits is an ongoing line of research without a closed amalgamation-class answer.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry of Polytopes and Polyhedra (Schulte, Handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the amalgamation problem for regular polytopes and lists open questions about extensions and flag orbits.
status_evidence.claim: The amalgamation problem and related flag-orbit boundedness questions are surveyed as open problems.
